facts.fact: Awakening means the wound's separate tears are beginning to act together. Missing conductors and forced bypass tests propagate pulses through an already failing network. The synchronized disturbance culminates in a connected violet horizon above Nexus and a threatened region-wide rupture. The Rift is not a newly conscious god, and ordinary arrivals are not causing this crisis.

The Severed Lands is objectively real. Every transported Riftborn arrived during an LSD trip in their outside world. Crossing is possible, never guaranteed; it predates the Rift wound and does not depend on its present deterioration. One local lifetime fits inside that original trip. Arrival obscures the crossing, not necessarily the person's name, skills or entire prior life.

Edda Rill organizes Returner relief and wants to rejoin the daughter she left in her outside world. She funded the Glasshouse bypass, accepting assurances that it was isolated. She initially denies that it harmed Thornwall. Specific correlated records and living victims can change her mind. If she persists after that evidence, she knowingly endangers others; longing for home does not make every Returner culpable.

The Nexus Root Gate is a surviving regulator under the Athenaeum, not an eighth newly invented surface Door. The Wind Archive atlas identifies its network circuits; the observatory manual restores their return controls. Defeat or lawfully override the Vigilant Engine, isolate the mass-passage bypass, then either restore regulated voluntary early return while maintaining containment or maintain containment with elective return shut. Both work. Forcing the bypass instead produces an uncontrolled rupture; it is not a secretly superior ending. The safe procedure requires no living sacrifice or optional quest item.

Anyone born in the Severed Lands, including children of one or two Riftborn, has an ordinary local life and death. They have no outside body and cannot return to a parent's world through these Doors. Normal Ruleset-supported death and revival apply; declare a Riftborn's return only when local death is permanent, not on reaching zero HP or while an applicable revival is still being pursued.

Natural return follows the end of a Riftborn's local life, including permanent adventuring death. Clear local memories barely survive; an emotional change and a fleeting sense of another lifetime may remain. Their actions and everyone left behind remain real. Return is not a repeatable reset or guaranteed second visit. A controlled early-return Door can end that life voluntarily before death; its safe operation must preserve the Anchors.

The Rift is one ancient dimensional wound with many visible tears. The Wardens caused it by attempting a permanent mass passage between worlds. Their Anchor network contains the wound and once also supported carefully controlled individual early returns. The Closed Vigil suspended elective passage during the disaster. Its custodians died before lifting the shutdown, leaving a deteriorating containment system. Natural arrivals and natural returns continued.

V authorized the Hearth Row bypass years ago, trusting a partial Warden translation. The experiment displaced the street and killed or stranded its residents. V stopped the work but concealed their authorship and what they knew about return. Their fear of another catastrophe is sincere; withholding the truth also protects them from accountability. They can assist under oversight, confess, obstruct or lose authority. V is an ordinary Riftborn, not an immortal Warden or a secret creator.
